**Status:** Final, tabled 21 August 2026
**Prepared by:** Group Strategy & Investor Relations

> `Harbourline Board Update H2 FY26 reformatted`. Every headline figure below

## 1. Group result

| Measure | H2 FY26 | H2 FY25 | Movement |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Group sales | $9,214.7m | $8,860.2m | +4.0% |
| Group EBIT | **$412.6m** | $389.4m | +6.0% |
| Cost of doing business (CODB) | **21.4%** | 22.0% | −60 bps |
| Net debt | **$1,046.2m** | $1,188.5m | −$142.3m |

## 2. Supply chain transformation

The DC-7 Truganina automation pilot is running at 1,180 cartons per hour
against a 1,450 design target. Phase 2 at Dandenong South has been deferred to
FY27. A go / no-go decision on DC-7 is scheduled for 9 October 2026.

Programme spend to date is $41.3m of the $96.0m three-year envelope.

## 3. Risks flagged to the board

1. **Single-source conveyor dependency.** No qualified second supplier for
   induction-lane drive units; 14-week replacement lead time.
2. **Peak-season freeze.** No production changes permitted from 3 November
   2026, compressing the remediation window after the go / no-go decision.
3. **Wage cost trajectory.** The enterprise agreement lands in Q3 FY27 and is
   modelled at a 3.9% increase; each 0.5% above that is $11.2m of annualised
   group cost.

## 4. Anticipated questions from the board

These are questions management expects to be asked at the 4 September 2026
board meeting. **They were compiled by the Group Strategy team. They are not
attributed to, and were not asked by, any individual director. No director has
been quoted anywhere in this pack.**

- Why has CODB improved while the DC-7 pilot is under-performing on
  throughput?
- What is the cost of holding phase 2 for a further financial year?
- If the service credit is not honoured, what is the recovery path?
- How exposed is the FY27 plan to the enterprise agreement outcome?
- What would trigger a decision to abandon the automation programme?

Management has **not** prepared draft answers to these questions. Answers are
to be given live by the accountable executive.
